req.title: load_logged_in_user populates g.user
req.statement: The system shall populate flask.g.user with the User row for the authenticated session on every request.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the system should populate flask.g.user with the User row for the authenticated session on every request. This behavior is critical for ensuring that user-specific actions are correctly attributed and authorized. The test suite will verify this functionality through positive, negative, and boundary cases to ensure robustness against common mutations.

tests.name: test_load_logged_in_user_positive
preconditions: User Rahul is registered in the system.
actions: Make a request to the index page.
expected: flask.g.user is populated with Rahul's user data.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Register and login user Rahul
client.post('/auth/register', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})

# Access index page
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
with app.app_context():
    assert g.user['username'] == 'Rahul'

tests.name: test_load_logged_in_user_negative
actions: Make a request to the index page.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Access index page without logging in
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
with app.app_context():
    assert g.user is None
